title: Vaginal swab test
what: The gynecologist takes a swab from the walls of the vagina and the cervix. It is checked under a microscope for inflammation and infection.
why: For unusual discharge, itching, or burning, at a checkup, during pregnancy, and before gynecology procedures.
duration: the procedure takes 1 to 2 minutes. Results usually take 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: The first day of your last period
If you recently took antibiotics or used vaginal suppositories
If you are pregnant or might be

prepare.title: Cycle
prepare.text: Not during your period. It is usually best in the first half of your cycle, after your period ends.

prepare.title: 2 days before
prepare.text: Usually no sex, douching, suppositories, creams, or vaginal tablets.

prepare.title: On the test day
prepare.text: Wash with warm water only, no soap or products. Sometimes you are asked not to pee for 2 to 3 hours before. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: If you are taking antibiotics, tell your doctor. They will decide the best time for the test.

bring: Socks or shoe covers, if your clinic asks for them
steps: You undress below the waist and lie on the exam chair
The doctor inserts a disposable speculum to see the cervix
A swab is taken with a soft brush or spatula
The sample is put on glass slides or into a tube
feel: Pressure and coolness from the speculum
It usually does not hurt. If it is uncomfortable, tell the doctor
after: You may have light spotting for the rest of the day. This is normal
You can usually go about your day as usual
red_flags: Severe pain in the lower belly or heavy bleeding after the procedure: see a doctor or call emergency services

faq.q: Can I have a swab during my period?
faq.a: No. Blood makes the result hard to read. It is usually done after your period ends.

faq.q: Can I have a swab if I have never had sex?
faq.a: Yes. Special thin instruments are used so the hymen is not damaged. Tell the doctor beforehand.

reminders.text: Vaginal swab in 2 days. From today, no sex, douching, suppositories, or creams.
